requirement:
The YAML outline exposes the following items beneath its file root:

| Construct | Kind | Name |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Block and flow mapping entries | `pair` | Written key |
| Block sequence entries | `item` | Anonymous |

Nested entries appear beneath their nearest enclosing outline item.
Selected source ends at the last non-comment token. Comment ownership follows
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`.

Item selectors, percent encoding, anonymous identities, and duplicate-name
suffixes follow {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`.
rationale:
The tests adequately cover `requirements.sdk.sources.yaml.items`.

**Block and flow mapping entries (`pair`, named by the written key).** `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs#fn[toml_and_yaml_profiles_name_keys]` checks the whole YAML outline summary: kind, name and line range for each item.
- Block mapping entries `a`, `c` and `e` appear as `pair[...]`.
- The quoted key appears as `pair["b"]`, so the key is named as written.
- The flow-mapping entry `d` in `{d: 1}` appears as `pair[d]`, nested under `pair[c]`.

**Block sequence entries (`item`, anonymous).** The same test checks that the two `- ...` entries under `e` appear as anonymous `item@` nodes. One of them holds a mapping, so the test also shows `item@/pair[f]`. Duplicate-name suffixes belong to the cited selector requirement and are not assessed here.

**Nesting beneath the nearest enclosing item.** The selector paths in that test show it: `pair["b"]/pair[e]/item@/pair[f]`. The line ranges, such as `pair["b"] 3-7`, show that each parent encloses its children.

**Selected source ends at the last non-comment token.** `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[yaml_selection_ends_before_trailing_comment_tokens]` uses `key: value # trailing comment`. It asserts that the selected text is exactly `key: value` and that the span is `0..10`.

**Comment ownership.** `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs#fn[yaml_comments_before_a_key_belong_to_that_key_not_the_previous_one]` covers the YAML-specific case. A comment line sits before a key at the same indentation, where the grammar folds it into the previous node. The test asserts that the comment belongs to `pair[jobs]/pair[second]`. `trailing_comments_outside: true` in the YAML `PROFILE` in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/languages/yaml.rs` is the profile setting this case exercises. The general ownership rules are cited from `requirements.references.outline_comments` and have their own tests.

**Residual risk.** There is no test where an own-line comment follows the last entry inside a nested block and the selected text must still end at the last token. The same trimming that the trailing-comment test exercises handles that case, so I do not count it as a separate gap.

**Selector grammar.** Percent encoding, anonymous identities and duplicate-name suffixes belong to `requirements.references.outline_selectors` (cited) and are not assessed here.

text: :::{req} items
The YAML outline exposes the following items beneath its file root:
| Construct | Kind | Name |
| Block and flow mapping entries | `pair` | Written key |
| Block sequence entries | `item` | Anonymous |
Nested entries appear beneath their nearest enclosing outline item.
Selected source ends at the last non-comment token. Comment ownership follows
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`.
Item selectors, percent encoding, anonymous identities, and duplicate-name
suffixes follow {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`.
:::{req} outline_comments
Each documented profile defines which grammar nodes are comments; the Markdown
profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph remains ordinary paragraph text. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. A reference in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.
:::{req} outline_selectors
Habeas uses the TBV [outline selector grammar](sdk/outlines.md#parse-an-outline-selector)
under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax` for source addresses.
